executive_summary.question: Under BNSS section 167, who may be deputed to make a local inquiry necessary under sections 164, 165 or 166, and what may that person be given?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
Under BNSS section 167(1), a **District Magistrate or a Sub‑divisional Magistrate** may depute **any Magistrate subordinate to him** to carry out a local inquiry required under sections 164, 165 or 166.  

The deputed Magistrate may be **furnished with written instructions** that are deemed necessary for his guidance (and the Magistrate may also declare who will bear the inquiry’s expenses).

evidence_analysis.supporting_evidence:
Exception.—This provision does not extend to the case in which the harbour is given
by the spouse of the deserter.

evidence_analysis.claim_text: The deputed Magistrate may be furnished with written instructions that are deemed necessary for his guidance.
evidence_analysis.supporting_evidence:
(1) Whenever a local inquiry is necessary for the purposes of section 164,
section 165 or section 166, a District Magistrate or Sub-divisional Magistrate may depute
any Magistrate subordinate to him to make the inquiry, and may furnish him with such
written instructions as may seem necessary for his guidance, and may declare by whom the
whole or any part of the necessary expenses of the inquiry shall be paid.
